dedupe_keys.name: climada hazard datasets for disaster risk assessment on hdx flood and earthquake selected countries

description: ETH Zürich publishes hazard sets from the CLIMADA risk platform on the Humanitarian Data Exchange for selected countries. The flood set gives footprints of historical flood events from 2000 to 2018 at 200 m resolution, based on the Cloud to Street flood database and processed into one hazard dataset per country. The earthquake set is at 150 arcseconds (about 4 km), globally and per country, from historic USGS epicentres from 1904 to 2017 plus a simple probabilistic sample of nine synthetic events per historic record, expressed as maximum Modified Mercalli intensity. The wildfire set is a global 4 km dataset based on MODIS satellite fire data from 2000 to 2021, described by Lüthi and others (2021) in Geoscientific Model Development. On HDX all three are provided as downloadable CSV summaries by first-level administrative area, including time series, for countries such as Afghanistan, Burkina Faso, Chad, Colombia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, under CC BY; the full hazard sets are available through the CLIMADA data API. Caveats: the providers ask users to judge suitability for each purpose, note that a 4 km grid is not suitable for neighbourhood-level risk, and state that the earthquake set has no peer-reviewed publication yet. It supports hazard exposure analysis and probabilistic risk modelling of infrastructure with CLIMADA; related records are the CLIMADA model and the Global Flood Database.
